name: jev_mem_stopping
description: Jev-Mem System-One read-side stopping decision. Port of memory/jev_questions.stopping_questions (4 noul) with the AND-of-STOP threshold logic from memory/jev_mem_retrieval.RetrievalController._query. Each rule matches one question (single condition) via `when.question`, ordered so that the first (most specific) CONTINUE reason wins — contradiction > missing_evidence > evidence_sufficient; if none fires, the fallthrough STOP_EVIDENCE_OK wins. This is the DSL idiom for `A && B && C => STOP` because `¬A ∨ ¬B ∨ ¬C => CONTINUE`.

evidence_sufficient.instructions: Does `evidence` contain support for every factual part of an answer to `query`?
evidence_sufficient.truthy: A grounded answer can be given from these memories without inventing missing facts.
evidence_sufficient.falsy: Any required fact or reasoning link is unsupported; related topics alone are insufficient.

continue_useful.instructions: Given `query` and `evidence`, is another retrieval round likely to fill a specific gap or resolve a conflict?
continue_useful.truthy: An identifiable missing fact or conflict could benefit from more memory retrieval.
continue_useful.falsy: No identifiable retrieval need remains or more memories are unlikely to help.

missing_evidence.instructions: Is at least one fact required by `query` absent from `evidence`?
missing_evidence.truthy: A required detail, date, identity, count or linking fact is not supported.
missing_evidence.falsy: All required facts have explicit support in the supplied evidence.

contradiction.instructions: Does `evidence` contain conflicting claims relevant to `query` that the supplied time/context cannot reconcile?
contradiction.truthy: A conflict still affects which answer is correct.
contradiction.falsy: Claims agree, differ only by explained temporal updates, or do not affect the answer.
